Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the complaint-notice text block in every policy jacket, acknowledgment letter and adverse-decision letter across all 51 jurisdictions; escalates disputed wording to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the complaint-record and consumer-notice provisions re-read at each form change: Alaska complaint-record requirement (rep jurisdiction, Alaska Division of Insurance contact block), plus Alabama, Arkansas and Connecticut complaint-record requirements; each state's current DOI consumer-services address, toll-free number and complaint URL re-verified from the DOI website on the drafting date

In-scope processes.value: Form and correspondence change intake → complaint-notice drafting → per-jurisdiction variant build → readability and legal clearance → form inventory update → SERFF filing hand-off, for every policy jacket, declarations page, complaint acknowledgment letter, claim denial letter and DOI-response cover letter

In-scope systems.value: Correspondence template library and form-selection rules in the policy administration platform; source-of-truth notice library in the document management repository; filed editions in SERFF

Compliance procedure documented.value: Complaint Notice & Disclosure Build Procedure — jurisdiction matrix build, variant drafting rules, DOI contact-data refresh, edition-date convention, filing trigger test

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel; re-approved on every DOI address/phone change bulletin and at least annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change — the notice edition must be approved and in the form inventory before the print/issuance freeze, and any jurisdiction that treats the complaint notice as a filed form must have the SERFF submission in before the target edition date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Form inventory milestone alerts at T-60/T-30/T-10 days to the target edition date, plus a standing quarterly reminder to re-verify all 51 DOI consumer-services contact blocks

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Form inventory extract, dated DOI contact-page captures, notice redlines, readability certificates and counsel clearance retained 7 years from withdrawal of the form edition

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any jurisdiction whose issued documents carry a stale DOI address, a missing complaint notice or an unapproved edition is logged as a forms exception with root cause, affected policy count and reissue decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every notice wording variant and every decision to reissue (or not reissue) documents that went out with a defective complaint notice

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All complaint-notice-bearing form editions and correspondence templates active in production during the year, by jurisdiction, line of business and writing company, per the form inventory

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a missing complaint notice or a wrong DOI address/phone in any jurisdiction; ≥1 such defect fails the test and triggers a reissue assessment; formatting-only defects (placement, font size) pass at ≤2% of sampled templates

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; testing runs on every release containing a notice change plus an annual 51-jurisdiction sweep of live templates

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must have authored no sampled notice variant and hold no role in the form inventory or SERFF filing process

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual complaint-notice content workpaper (jurisdiction matrix, template extract, sampled proofs, DOI contact verification captures) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Form inventory export showing notice text, edition date and effective dates by jurisdiction, with sample issued documents — producible for a market conduct exam forms request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager answers DOI forms criticisms; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a defective notice and any corrective-mailing commitment before it leaves

checklist.step: Open the notice change and fix its jurisdiction scope
actions: Take the change request from the Insurance Product Manager or the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and record the driver: new DOI address, new statutory wording, new product, or exam criticism.
In the policy administration platform open Configuration ▸ Correspondence ▸ Template Library and filter on templates carrying the COMPLAINT-NOTICE tag to list every artifact in play.
Write the affected jurisdictions onto the change record — default is all 51 (50 states plus DC) unless the driver is a single-state bulletin.

Record for each artifact whether it is a policy jacket, declarations page, complaint acknowledgment letter, adverse-decision/denial letter or DOI response cover letter, and which writing companies use it.
Attach the change record to a new notice-build folder named REG-027-C01-<yyyy-mm-dd> in the document management repository.
checklist.done: the change record names the driver, the jurisdiction list and every affected template with its artifact type and writing companies.

checklist.step: Pull the current complaint-notice requirement for each jurisdiction
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System open REG-027 Complaint Handling & Record and export the per-jurisdiction requirement rows.

For the representative jurisdiction, read the Alaska complaint-record requirement in full and note what the Alaska Division of Insurance expects on consumer-facing documents; repeat for the Alabama, Arkansas and Connecticut supporting citations.

For every remaining jurisdiction, open the DOI's consumer-complaint page and capture the mandated notice language, required placement (policy jacket vs first page of the denial letter) and any required font/prominence rule.
Print each source page to PDF as <state>-complaint-notice-source-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it in the notice-build folder — this is the evidence behind the wording.
checklist.done: a dated source capture and a stated wording/placement requirement exist for all 51 jurisdictions.

checklist.step: Re-verify the DOI consumer-services contact block for all 51 jurisdictions
actions: For each jurisdiction open the DOI website's Consumer Services / File a Complaint page and read off the mailing address, toll-free consumer number, TTY line, email and online complaint URL.

Cross-check the same details against the NAIC Consumer Information Source state contact list and against the address printed on the last transmittal letter the Complaints Manager received from that DOI.
Where the three sources disagree, phone the DOI consumer-services line, confirm the current block and log the call date, the person spoken to and the answer on the matrix row.
Record for Alaska: the Alaska Division of Insurance Consumer Services address, its consumer hotline and its online complaint URL, as read on the verification date.
Mark each row Verified <date> by <name>; no row may carry a contact block older than one quarter.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction row shows a contact block verified within the quarter, with the source and any DOI phone confirmation logged.

checklist.step: Build the 51-jurisdiction notice matrix
actions: Create one matrix row per jurisdiction with columns: required wording, citation, placement, prominence rule, DOI contact block, filed-form flag, artifact types affected, variant id.
Group jurisdictions that accept identical wording into a single base variant and give each genuine deviation its own variant id (for example AK-01, CA-01).
Flag every jurisdiction whose notice must be filed as part of the policy form so it routes to the SERFF hand-off step.
Hand the matrix to Regulatory Counsel and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for a first read before drafting starts.
checklist.done: the matrix carries 51 complete rows, a variant id per row and a filed-form flag, and has been read by Counsel and Market Conduct.

checklist.step: Draft the base notice text and each jurisdiction variant
actions: Draft the base block: how to complain to the company (complaints unit address, toll-free number, email, portal link), then how to complain to the DOI with that jurisdiction's verified contact block.
Reproduce any jurisdiction's prescribed wording verbatim — never paraphrase text a statute prescribes; paste it from the dated source capture.
Merge the verified contact block into each variant using the matrix, and state the company complaints unit's own acknowledgment commitment consistent with what REG-027-C02 actually delivers.
Save each variant in the document management repository as NOTICE-COMPLAINT-<variant id>-v<n>.docx with the matrix row referenced in the document properties.
checklist.done: every variant id in the matrix has a drafted notice that reproduces prescribed wording verbatim and carries the verified contact block.

checklist.step: Clear the drafted text with Regulatory Counsel against the cited statute
actions: Read each variant side by side with its dated source capture and the citation on the matrix row.
Confirm prescribed wording is verbatim, that nothing added narrows the consumer's right to complain to the DOI, and that no variant promises a response time the company cannot meet.
Reject and return any variant whose contact block is unverified or whose citation is to a superseded provision, naming the defect.
Stamp cleared variants with counsel name and clearance date in the document properties and record the clearance on the matrix row.
checklist.done: every variant carries a dated counsel clearance or has been returned with a named defect.

checklist.step: Run readability and accessibility checks on the notice block
actions: Score each variant for Flesch Reading Ease and record the score against the jurisdiction's readability floor for policy forms (commonly 40–50 where a floor exists).
Check the rendered block against each jurisdiction's prominence rule: minimum point size, bold/caps requirement and position on the page.
Check the block survives the Spanish-language rendition where the jurisdiction requires one, and hand translations to the Content Specialist with a due date.
Attach the readability certificate and the rendered proof to the matrix row.
checklist.done: each variant has a recorded readability score, a prominence check against its jurisdiction rule and, where required, a translated rendition.

checklist.step: Update the form inventory with the new editions
actions: For every affected form and template add or update the inventory row: form number, edition date (MM-YY as printed in the form footer), variant id, jurisdictions, writing companies, artifact type, filed/not-filed, superseded edition.
Set the superseded edition's end date to the day before the new edition's effective date so no jurisdiction has a gap or an overlap.
Link each inventory row to the cleared variant file and to the dated source capture behind it.
Have the Records Manager confirm the superseded edition is retained rather than overwritten.
checklist.done: the form inventory shows exactly one live complaint-notice edition per jurisdiction per artifact type, with linked source and clearance evidence.

checklist.step: Route the filed-form jurisdictions to a SERFF submission
actions: Take every matrix row flagged filed-form and open the state's entry under Industry ▸ Filing Rules in SERFF to read the review method and the required transmittal for a notice-only form change.

Create the SERFF filing with the correct TOI/Sub-TOI, attach the print-ready notice PDF, the redline against the superseded edition and a cover letter stating the change is the complaint-notice block only.
Compute the latest submission date as the target edition date minus the state's review/deemer days minus a 10-business-day objection buffer, and submit ahead of it.
Write the SERFF Tracking Number back onto the matrix row and the form inventory row, and set the jurisdiction to blocked-from-use until disposition or a satisfied deemer.
checklist.done: every filed-form jurisdiction has a SERFF submission with a tracking number recorded and a use-block until disposition.

checklist.step: Bind each variant to its correspondence templates
actions: In the policy administration platform open Configuration ▸ Correspondence ▸ Template Library and map variant id to template for every artifact type and jurisdiction.
Set the selection rule keys — risk state (not mailing state), line of business, writing company and document date — so the correct variant merges automatically.
Bind the same variants in the claims correspondence set used for denial and adverse-decision letters, coordinating with the Claims Quality Assurance / Training Manager.
Record the configuration in a change ticket so REG-027-C03 can control and test the deployment.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction/artifact combination resolves to exactly one variant through a documented selection rule, captured on a change ticket.

checklist.step: Proof the merged output before release
actions: Generate one merged proof per jurisdiction per artifact type in the pre-production environment using a test policy and a test complaint case.
Read the rendered notice block on each proof against the matrix row: wording verbatim, contact block correct, placement and point size within the prominence rule, no truncation at page breaks.
Generate proofs in both PDF and print-stream output so print-vendor rendering defects surface before mailing.
Log each defect against the template with a screenshot and a jurisdiction, and re-proof after the fix.
checklist.done: a clean proof exists for every jurisdiction and artifact type in both PDF and print-stream output.

checklist.step: Publish the notice library and retire the superseded editions
actions: Publish the cleared variants to the controlled notice library and mark them Effective <date> with the matrix and counsel clearance attached.
Move superseded editions to Retired, keeping them retrievable by form number and edition date for the retention period.
Remove uncontrolled copies from team SharePoint sites and the print vendor's staging folder so nobody prints a retired block.
Notify the print/fulfilment vendor in writing of the effective date and confirm they acknowledge the stock cut-over.
checklist.done: the controlled library shows one effective edition per variant, superseded editions are retired but retrievable, and the print vendor has acknowledged the cut-over.

checklist.step: Tell the downstream teams what changed and when it bites
actions: Send the Complaints Manager, Contact Center Ops Manager, Claims Director / Manager and Policy Admin Ops Lead a change note listing affected jurisdictions, artifacts, effective date and what a reader will now see.
Give the Complaints Specialist team the new variant text so verbal referrals to the DOI match the printed block.
Hand the Instructional Designer the change note as an input to the REG-027-C04 annual training refresh.
File the change note in the notice-build folder.
checklist.done: complaints, contact centre, claims and policy admin leads have a dated change note naming jurisdictions, artifacts and the effective date.

checklist.step: Assess whether documents already issued need a corrective notice
actions: Where the change was driven by a defect (stale DOI address, missing block), ask the Policy Administration Analyst for the count of policies and letters issued with the defective edition, by jurisdiction and date range.
Decide in writing per jurisdiction: corrective mailing, notice at next renewal, or no action, with the reasoning and the statute relied on.
Where a corrective mailing is chosen, set the mailing date and hand the population to the Correspondence Clerk with the approved cover letter.
Decide with the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager whether the defect is self-reported to any DOI, and record that decision.
checklist.done: every defect-driven change has a written, counsel-signed remediation decision per jurisdiction, with a mailing date or a stated basis for no action.

checklist.step: File the build evidence for retention
actions: Move the notice-build folder — matrix, dated source and DOI contact captures, drafts, counsel clearances, readability certificates, proofs, SERFF tracking numbers, change note — into the compliance evidence repository under REG-027-C01 and the edition date.
Apply the 7-years-from-edition-withdrawal retention label so the record outlives the form.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by jurisdiction, form number, edition date and variant id.
Have the Policy Forms Specialist sign the folder as complete.
checklist.done: the build record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, searchable by jurisdiction and form number, and signed complete.

testing.step: Build the population of live complaint-notice artifacts
actions: Extract from the policy administration platform every correspondence template and form edition tagged COMPLAINT-NOTICE that was effective at any point in the audit year, by jurisdiction, artifact type and writing company.
Add the claims denial/adverse-decision letter set from the claims platform so claim-side artifacts cannot hide.
Expect 51 jurisdictions × each artifact type; list any jurisdiction/artifact cell with no live artifact as an immediate exception.
Sign the extract as complete and record the extraction date and query used.
testing.done: the population covers every jurisdiction/artifact cell, empty cells are already flagged, and the extract is signed and dated.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the form inventory and SERFF
actions: Match every extracted artifact to a form inventory row on form number plus edition date.
List artifacts live in production with no inventory row, and inventory rows with no live artifact, as reconciling items and clear each one with the Policy Forms Specialist.
For every inventory row flagged filed-form, confirm a SERFF Tracking Number is recorded and the disposition pre-dates the edition effective date.
Carry unresolved reconciling items straight into the exception log rather than adjusting the population.
testing.done: production, form inventory and SERFF agree, or every difference is logged as an exception with an owner.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of jurisdictions whose notice wording is statutorily prescribed verbatim, and 100% of jurisdictions changed during the year.
Add a seeded random selection of 25 remaining jurisdiction/artifact cells, for a minimum sample of 40 cells.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selection tool in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Pull the merged output proof and the underlying variant file for each sampled cell.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all prescribed-wording and changed jurisdictions, and each cell has its proof and variant attached.

testing.step: Re-perform the wording test against the regulator's own text
actions: For each sampled jurisdiction open that DOI's consumer-complaint page and the cited statute yourself and read the required wording before looking at the company variant.
Compare word for word where the wording is prescribed; treat any paraphrase, omission or added qualifier as a fail.
For Alaska, test the block against the Alaska complaint-record requirement and the Alaska Division of Insurance consumer page; repeat for the Alabama, Arkansas and Connecticut supporting citations.
Screenshot the regulator page you relied on into the workpaper with the date visible.
testing.done: each sampled jurisdiction has an independent wording conclusion supported by a dated capture of the regulator's own page.

testing.step: Verify the DOI contact block on the artifact actually reaches the DOI
actions: Compare the printed address, toll-free number and complaint URL on the sampled proof to the DOI's current published block and to the NAIC Consumer Information Source listing.
Open each printed complaint URL and confirm it resolves to that DOI's live complaint form, not a redirect or a dead page.
Dial a sample of at least five printed toll-free numbers and confirm they reach the DOI consumer services line; log the date and result.
Treat any unreachable number or dead URL as a content fail regardless of when it was last verified.
testing.done: every sampled contact block is confirmed live, with URL resolution and phone checks logged.

testing.step: Trace proofs through to documents genuinely issued to consumers
actions: For each sampled jurisdiction pull three real issued documents from the document archive — one policy jacket, one complaint acknowledgment, one denial letter — dated after the edition effective date.
Read the complaint block on the issued image and compare it to the approved variant, checking for truncation, overprint and missing pages in the print stream.
Where the issued document carries a superseded edition, capture the issue date and quantify how many documents used it.
Attach the issued-document images to the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled jurisdictions are traced to real issued documents carrying the approved edition, or the superseded-edition volume is quantified.

testing.step: Recompute the edition-date and effective-date maths
actions: For each changed jurisdiction recompute: superseded edition end date = new edition effective date − 1 day, and confirm the inventory holds that.
For filed-form jurisdictions recompute the latest submission date as edition date − review/deemer days − 10-business-day objection buffer, and compare to the actual SERFF submission date.
Confirm no jurisdiction issued the new edition before its SERFF disposition or satisfied deemer date.
Treat use before approval as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: edition gaps, overlaps and any pre-approval use are quantified, with the deemer maths reconciled per filed jurisdiction.

testing.step: Test the control record behind the sampled variants
actions: For each sampled variant pull the dated source capture, the counsel clearance stamp and the readability certificate from the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm the source capture pre-dates the drafting date and the counsel clearance pre-dates the edition effective date.
Confirm the contact-block verification on the matrix row is dated within the quarter preceding the edition.
Treat a correct notice with no dated source capture as a control fail, separate from any content result.
testing.done: every sampled variant has a pre-dated source capture, counsel clearance and in-quarter contact verification, or a control fail is recorded.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying jurisdiction, artifact, defect type (missing block, stale contact, paraphrased wording, unfiled edition, control gap) and the consumer-document volume affected.
Assign a root cause — DOI contact change missed, variant not bound to the template, print-stream truncation, filing not made — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for missing-notice or stale-address defects, open a reissue assessment with Regulatory Counsel under the C01 remediation step.
Mark every open exception as a mandatory retest row in the next sweep.
testing.done: every exception carries a jurisdiction, defect type, affected volume, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest flag.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the content defect rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missing notices and wrong contact blocks, and the ≤2% allowance for formatting-only defects.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have a Compliance Officer who authored no sampled variant sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any reissue decisions to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the defect rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, and is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the response to every DOI-forwarded complaint inside the statutory period and the consumer acknowledgment that precedes it; escalates at-risk cases to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the response-period provisions re-read at intake for each forwarding state: Alaska complaint-record requirement (Alaska Division of Insurance transmittal, customarily 20 days), Arizona (15 working days), California (10 CCR 2695.5(b), 21 calendar days for claim-related DOI inquiries), plus the Alabama, Arkansas and Connecticut complaint-record requirements; the due date printed on the transmittal letter always governs where it is shorter

In-scope processes.value: DOI complaint transmittal intake → same-day register entry → consumer acknowledgment → business-unit position statement → DOI response letter → transmittal through the state channel → disposition coding and closure, for every complaint forwarded by any of the 51 DOIs and every direct consumer complaint escalated to a DOI

In-scope systems.value: Complaint case records, SLA clocks and correspondence generation in the workflow/case management tool; inbound transmittals via NAIC State Based Systems complaint module, state DOI portals and the monitored complaints mailbox; outbound letters archived to the document management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: DOI Complaint Response Procedure — same-day logging, due-date computation from the transmittal letter, position-statement SLA, mandatory response content, extension protocol, disposition coding

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; re-approved annually and whenever a DOI changes its response window or forwarding channel

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per complaint — the response is due on the date printed on the DOI transmittal letter, defaulted to the state's statutory window where none is printed (Alaska 20 days, Arizona 15 working days, California 21 calendar days); the case clock starts on the transmittal date, not the date it reached the mailbox

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case alerts at due date −7, −3 and −1 days to the assigned Complaints Specialist and at −3 days to the Complaints Manager; a daily aged-case report lists everything inside 5 days of due and everything overdue

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Transmittal letter, acknowledgment, position statement, DOI response letter with enclosures, transmission proof and closure coding retained as the complaint file for 5 years from closure (current plus prior five exam cycles)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any response transmitted after the due date, or with an extension not granted in writing, is logged as a late-response exception with the day count, root cause and the DOI's reaction

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late response, every extension request and every response that admits an error or offers restitution

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All DOI-forwarded complaints received in the test quarter across the 51 jurisdictions per the complaint register, including reopened cases and cases closed without a substantive response

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a response transmitted after the due date without a written extension; ≥1 late response fails the test; missing mandatory content elements in the response letter fail at >2% of the sample

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven per complaint; testing runs quarterly over that quarter's complaints, with 100% review of any complaint that went overdue

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must have handled none of the sampled complaints and sit outside the complaints handling queue

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly complaint-response timeliness workpaper (register extract, transmittal reconciliation, sample, due-date recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Complaint register export plus the full complaint file for any case number a DOI names — transmittal, response, enclosures and transmission proof — producible for a market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Complaints Manager answers the forwarding DOI directly; the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager handles exam criticisms and Regulatory Counsel clears any response admitting a statutory violation

checklist.step: Take in the DOI transmittal and log it the day it arrives
actions: Sweep the three inbound channels every business morning: the NAIC State Based Systems complaint module inbox, the state DOI portals the company is registered on, and the monitored complaints@ mailbox and fax queue.

Open a case in the workflow/case management tool the same business day and key: DOI case/file number, forwarding state, transmittal date, date received, complainant name, policy or claim number, the DOI analyst's name and direct contact.
Attach the transmittal letter and every enclosure to the case, and record the response due date exactly as printed on the letter.
Where the transmittal is illegible or missing an enclosure, email the named DOI analyst the same day for the missing item and log the request on the case.
Never let a transmittal sit in a mailbox overnight — the clock runs from the DOI's transmittal date, not from your intake.
checklist.done: every transmittal received that day has a case with the DOI file number, transmittal date, printed due date and the letter attached.

checklist.step: Compute and set the response clock
actions: Take the due date printed on the transmittal letter as the governing date.

Where no date is printed, compute it from the state rule on the case: Alaska 20 days from the Alaska Division of Insurance transmittal date, Arizona 15 working days, California 21 calendar days under 10 CCR 2695.5(b), and the state-specific window for every other jurisdiction from the Internal Regulatory System.
State on the case whether the window counts calendar days, business days or working days, and whether it runs from the transmittal date or the receipt date.
Set the internal target at due date − 3 business days so review and transmittal fit inside the window, and confirm the −7/−3/−1 day alerts fired onto the case.
checklist.done: the case carries a governing due date, the day-count basis, the statutory source and an internal target three business days earlier, with alerts armed.

checklist.step: Assign the case and acknowledge to the consumer
actions: Assign the case to a Complaints Specialist who did not handle the underlying transaction, based on line of business and current caseload from the queue dashboard.

Have the assignee send the consumer a written acknowledgment within 2 business days, using the approved acknowledgment template that carries the REG-027-C01 complaint notice block for the complainant's state.
Name the handler and give a direct phone number and email in the acknowledgment so the consumer is not routed back to the general line.
Attach the acknowledgment to the case and record its send date on the register row.
checklist.done: the case has a conflict-free assignee and a dated consumer acknowledgment sent within 2 business days, both recorded on the register.

checklist.step: Pull the underlying policy, billing and claim record
actions: Look up the policy in the policy administration platform and export the transaction history: issue, endorsements, cancellations, reinstatements, billing notices and lapse notices with their generation dates.
Where the complaint is claim-related, pull the claim file, diary notes, reserve history, coverage position and every letter sent from the claims platform.
Pull the contact-centre call recordings and chat transcripts for the disputed dates from the contact centre platform and note the times.
Build a dated fact chronology on the case that a DOI analyst could follow without asking a follow-up question.
checklist.done: the case holds a dated chronology backed by policy, claim and contact-centre records covering every date the complainant raised.

checklist.step: Get the business unit's position statement inside the internal SLA
actions: Send the owning unit — Underwriting, Claims, Billing or Distribution — a position request naming the disputed decision, the documents needed and an internal due date of 5 business days before the DOI due date.
Require the unit to state the decision, the policy provision or rule relied on, whether the decision stands, and whether any error occurred.
Escalate a missed internal SLA to that unit's manager the next business day and log the escalation on the case; never absorb the delay into the DOI window.
Attach the position statement and its supporting documents to the case.
checklist.done: a written position statement citing the governing provision is on the case at least 5 business days before the DOI due date, or an escalation is logged.

checklist.step: Test the position before adopting it
actions: Read the cited policy provision in the actual issued form edition for the risk state, not the current filed edition, and confirm it says what the unit claims.
Check the decision against the state's unfair claims settlement practices and consumer-protection standards captured in the Internal Regulatory System.
Where the position is wrong or unsupported, send it back to the unit the same day with the defect named, and tell the Complaints Manager the due date is now at risk.
Where an error is confirmed, propose the remedy — reinstatement, reissue, refund with interest, claim reopening — with the amount computed.
checklist.done: the adopted position is verified against the issued form edition and the state standard, with any error and its computed remedy stated.

checklist.step: Draft the DOI response letter with every mandatory element
actions: Use the approved DOI response template and address it to the named DOI analyst with the DOI file number and the company case number in the reference line.

Include: the complainant and policy/claim identifiers, a dated chronology, the company position, the specific policy provision or statute relied on with its text quoted, the action taken or offered with amounts and dates, and a named contact for follow-up.
Attach the enclosures the DOI asked for — declarations page, issued form edition, letters sent, payment records — indexed and paginated so a reference can be found.
Answer every question the transmittal asked, in the order asked; a response that leaves a numbered DOI question unanswered is not complete.
Redact third-party personal data that is not the complainant's before enclosing.
checklist.done: the draft answers every transmittal question, cites the governing provision, states the action taken and carries indexed enclosures.

checklist.step: Review and clear the response before it is transmitted
actions: Read the draft against the transmittal letter and confirm every question is answered and every cited provision matches the issued form edition.
Route to Regulatory Counsel any response that admits a statutory violation, denies coverage on a contested ground, or offers restitution above the delegated threshold.
Check the tone: no argumentative language directed at the DOI or the consumer, no admission the facts do not support.
Stamp the case with the reviewer name and clearance date; an uncleared draft may not be transmitted.
checklist.done: the response carries a dated reviewer clearance and, where required, Regulatory Counsel clearance before transmittal.

checklist.step: Transmit through the channel the DOI specified and keep the proof
actions: Send through the channel named on the transmittal — upload to the NAIC State Based Systems complaint module or the state DOI portal, or reply to the analyst's email address; do not substitute a channel.
Capture the transmission proof: portal confirmation screen with the timestamp and confirmation number, or the sent-email header, and attach it to the case.
Where the portal rejects an attachment on size or format, split or convert it and re-upload the same day, logging the retry.
Record the actual transmission date on the register and compare it to the due date; if it is late, open the late-response exception immediately.
checklist.done: the response is transmitted through the DOI's named channel with a timestamped confirmation attached and the transmission date on the register.

checklist.step: Send the consumer their copy and the closing letter
actions: Send the complainant a copy of the position communicated to the DOI in plain language on the same day the DOI response goes out, unless the state forbids direct contact during its review.
Include the complaint-notice block for the complainant's state from the C01 controlled library so their onward rights are stated.
Where a remedy was agreed, state the amount, the payment method and the date it will be issued, and open the payment task with Billing or Claims.
Archive both letters to the document management repository indexed by case number, policy number and state.
checklist.done: the complainant has a same-day plain-language copy with the state notice block and, where relevant, a dated remedy commitment; both letters are archived.

checklist.step: Request an extension in writing when the window genuinely cannot be met
actions: Where the position cannot be completed by due date − 3 business days, contact the named DOI analyst before the due date, never after it.
Ask in writing, stating what is outstanding, why, and a specific committed date; keep the ask to one extension.
Attach the DOI's written grant to the case and reset the due date to the granted date, keeping the original date visible on the register.
Where the DOI refuses, transmit an interim response by the original due date stating the facts established so far and the date the balance will follow.
checklist.done: no case passes its due date without either a transmitted response, a written DOI extension on file, or a transmitted interim response.

checklist.step: Work the DOI's follow-up questions on the original clock discipline
actions: Log every DOI follow-up as a new activity on the same case with its own transmittal date and printed due date.
Re-open the position with the business unit where the follow-up raises new facts, using the same 5-business-day internal SLA.
Transmit the supplemental response through the same channel and attach the new confirmation.
Do not close the case while any DOI question is outstanding, even if the DOI has issued a preliminary finding.
checklist.done: every DOI follow-up has its own dated activity, due date and transmitted supplemental response on the case.

checklist.step: Code the disposition and close the register row
actions: Set the NAIC-aligned coding on the register row: line of coverage, function code (underwriting, marketing & sales, policyholder service, claims), reason code (denial of claim, delays, unsatisfactory settlement, premium/rating, cancellation/nonrenewal) and disposition.
Record the outcome — company position upheld, claim reopened, additional payment, policy reinstated, refund issued — with the dollar amount where money moved.
Record the closure date and the DOI's own disposition once it publishes one, and the elapsed days from transmittal to response.
Reject a closure that leaves function code, reason code or disposition blank — these feed the MCAS submission and the market analysis.
checklist.done: the register row carries function code, reason code, disposition, outcome, any amount, and the transmittal-to-response day count, with no blanks.

checklist.step: Work the daily aged-case report until it is clear
actions: Open the daily complaint aging dashboard and read the three buckets: due within 5 days, due within 2 days, and overdue.
Contact the assigned specialist on every case in the 2-day bucket and record on the case what is outstanding and who owns it.
Escalate anything overdue to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager the same day with a recovery date.
Report the count of overdue cases by state weekly to the Head of Compliance; the target is zero and any non-zero week carries a written cause.
checklist.done: the aging dashboard is worked daily, every 2-day-bucket case has a named owner and outstanding item, and overdue cases are escalated the same day.

checklist.step: File the complete complaint file for retention
actions: On closure, move the complaint file — transmittal, acknowledgment, chronology, position statement, cleared response, enclosures, transmission proof, consumer copy, disposition coding — into the compliance evidence repository under state and case number.
Apply the 5-years-from-closure retention label and place a legal hold on any case tied to litigation or an open market conduct exam.
Confirm the file is retrievable by DOI file number, company case number, policy number, state and reason code.
Have the Complaints Manager sign the file as complete before it is locked.
checklist.done: the closed file is complete, labelled for 5-year retention, retrievable by DOI file number and signed off.

testing.step: Build the population of DOI complaints received in the quarter
actions: Extract from the workflow/case management tool every complaint case with a DOI transmittal date inside the quarter, by state, line of business and writing company.
Add reopened cases and cases closed without a substantive response so nothing drops out of scope.
Record for each row: transmittal date, receipt date, printed due date, transmission date, disposition, function and reason codes.
Sign the extract as complete with the extraction date and query recorded.
testing.done: the population covers every DOI complaint transmitted in the quarter including reopens, and the extract is signed and dated.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to what the regulators actually sent
actions: Pull the inbound list from the NAIC State Based Systems complaint module and each state DOI portal the company is registered on for the same quarter.
Sweep the monitored complaints mailbox and fax log for transmittals with no matching case.
Match on DOI file number; every transmittal with no case is an automatic exception — an unlogged complaint cannot have been answered on time.
Resolve or log every difference before sampling; do not adjust the population to make it tie.
testing.done: every DOI transmittal in the quarter is matched to a case or logged as an unlogged-complaint exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample
actions: Take 100% of cases that went overdue, 100% of cases with a written extension, and 100% of claim-denial reason-code cases.
Add 30 cases selected at random with a recorded seed from the remainder, stratified so every state that sent more than five complaints is represented, minimum 45 cases total.
Record seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper so the sample is reproducible.
Pull the full complaint file for each sampled case.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all overdue, extended and denial cases, and each case file is in hand.

testing.step: Recompute the response due date independently
actions: Read the due date off the transmittal letter image yourself rather than off the case field.

Where no date is printed, recompute from the state rule — Alaska 20 days from the Alaska Division of Insurance transmittal date, Arizona 15 working days, California 21 calendar days under 10 CCR 2695.5(b) — using the correct calendar/business/working-day basis and the state's holiday calendar.
Compare your recomputed date to the date recorded on the case; any difference is an exception even where the response still landed on time.
Record the recomputation for each sampled case in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independently recomputed due date and a stated agreement or difference against the recorded date.

testing.step: Test the transmission date against the due date using the proof, not the case field
actions: Open the transmission proof — the NAIC State Based Systems or state portal confirmation screen, or the sent-email header — and read the timestamp.
Compare that timestamp to the governing due date and compute the days early or late; do not rely on the case's transmission-date field.
Where an extension is claimed, confirm the DOI's written grant is attached and pre-dates the original due date.
Treat any response transmitted after the due date with no pre-dated written grant as a fail against the zero-tolerance threshold.
testing.done: every sampled response has a proof-based transmission timestamp and a computed days-early/late figure against the governing due date.

testing.step: Test the response letter for the mandatory content elements
actions: Read each sampled transmittal, list its numbered questions, and confirm the response answers each one.
Confirm the response states the policy provision or statute relied on and quotes it, names the action taken or offered with amounts and dates, and gives a named contact.
Open the issued form edition for that policy and confirm the quoted provision matches the edition in force, not the current filed edition.
Confirm third-party personal data was redacted from the enclosures; treat an unredacted enclosure as a privacy exception routed to the Privacy Officer.
testing.done: each sampled response is scored element by element, with unanswered questions, misquoted provisions and unredacted enclosures listed.

testing.step: Verify the consumer acknowledgment and closing letter went out
actions: Pull the acknowledgment image from the document management repository and confirm its send date is within 2 business days of the case open date.
Confirm the acknowledgment and the closing letter carry the current complaint-notice block for the complainant's state from the C01 controlled library.
Confirm the closing letter went the same day as the DOI response and, where a remedy was promised, trace the payment to the billing or claims payment record with its date and amount.
List any case with no acknowledgment, a stale notice block or an unpaid promised remedy.
testing.done: acknowledgments, closing letters and promised payments are traced to dated evidence for every sampled case.

testing.step: Test the disposition coding that feeds market-conduct reporting
actions: Read each sampled complaint file and assign your own function code, reason code and line of coverage before looking at the recorded coding.
Compare to the register row; a miscoded reason code is an exception because it flows into the NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement complaint counts.
Confirm no sampled row has a blank function code, reason code, disposition or closure date.
Recompute the transmittal-to-response day count on the row and confirm it matches the proof timestamps.
testing.done: coding is independently re-performed on every sampled case, with miscodings and blanks listed and day counts reconciled.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the DOI file number, state, defect type (late response, unlogged complaint, missing element, miscoding, no acknowledgment) and days late where relevant.
Assign a root cause — transmittal not swept, business unit missed the internal SLA, clock set from receipt instead of transmittal date, channel rejection not retried — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for late responses, decide with the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager whether the forwarding DOI needs a written explanation.
Flag every open exception as a mandatory retest row in next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has a DOI file number, defect type, day count, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest flag.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the late-response count against the zero-tolerance threshold and the content-element defect rate against the 2% allowance.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references, and break the late count out by state so repeat jurisdictions are visible.
Have a reviewer who handled none of the sampled complaints sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion, late responses by state and open remediations to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the late count by state, the content defect rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, and is filed.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — every configured response window is traced to a named source before it is coded: the Alaska complaint-record requirement and the Alaska Division of Insurance transmittal practice (20 days), Arizona 15 working days, California 10 CCR 2695.5(b) 21 calendar days, plus the Alabama, Arkansas and Connecticut complaint-record requirements; the configuration table records citation and verification date per state

In-scope processes.value: Configuration change intake → per-state SLA rule build → mandatory-field and coding-list build → correspondence template binding → lower-environment test → change-advisory approval → production release → post-release validation, for the complaint case type across all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Complaint case type, SLA rule table, mandatory field set and NAIC function/reason code lists in the workflow/case management tool, with change control in the ITSM platform and correspondence templates sourced from the policy administration platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Complaint System Configuration Standard — SLA table schema, day-count basis and holiday-calendar rules, mandatory-field enforcement, code-list governance, template binding, regression pack, back-out plan

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the IT Service Delivery Manager and the Head of Compliance jointly; re-approved on every platform upgrade and whenever a state changes its response window

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change — an SLA table change must be in production before the effective date of the state's new window, and no complaint may be opened under a stale rule; the quarterly configuration attestation is due within 10 business days of quarter end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Change-ticket alerts at T-14/T-7/T-2 days to the state rule effective date, plus a monthly automated diff that flags any state whose configured window no longer matches the Internal Regulatory System entry

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Configuration export, SLA table with per-state citations, test evidence, change approval, release record and post-release validation retained 7 years, with the pre-change baseline kept alongside each release

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any production configuration differing from the approved baseline, any unapproved emergency change and any state whose configured window is wrong is raised as a configuration exception with the affected case count

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every SLA rule change, every emergency change to complaint configuration and the remediation of any case opened under a wrong window

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All 51 configured state SLA rows plus every complaint-configuration release deployed in the period, per the ITSM change log and the configuration export

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a wrong configured response window or a disabled mandatory field; any single wrong state row fails the test; cosmetic configuration drift (label text, sort order) passes at ≤5% of rows

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; testing runs on every complaint-configuration release plus a quarterly full 51-row SLA reconciliation against the Internal Regulatory System

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must neither have specified nor approved the sampled configuration changes and must not be the implementer

Evidence location for test results.value: Release test pack and quarterly configuration reconciliation workpaper (baseline export, diff report, test-case results, defect list) attached to the change ticket and copied to the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Configuration export showing the response window, citation and verification date per state, with change approvals and test evidence — producible for a market conduct exam IT request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager answers exam questions on system controls with the Business Systems Analyst supplying configuration evidence; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement about cases handled under a misconfigured rule

checklist.step: Take in the configuration change and raise a controlled ticket
actions: Open a normal change ticket in the ITSM platform naming the driver: a state window change, a new NAIC reason code, a template rebind from REG-027-C01, or an exam finding.
Record on the ticket the affected states, the complaint case type, the configuration objects touched and the required production date.
Attach the requirement from the Complaints Manager or the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager in writing — no verbal configuration requests.
Link the ticket to the REG-027 obligation in the Internal Regulatory System so the change is traceable to the obligation it serves.
checklist.done: a change ticket exists with the driver, affected states, objects, required date, written requirement and a link to REG-027.

checklist.step: Export and freeze the current configuration baseline
actions: Export the complaint case type configuration from production: SLA rule table, mandatory field set, function and reason code lists, escalation rules and template bindings.
Save the export as BASELINE-<ticket>-<yyyy-mm-dd> and attach it to the change ticket — this is the back-out reference.
Record the platform version and the environment build number alongside the export.
Confirm the baseline is byte-identical to the last approved release export; any unexplained difference is drift and goes to the exception log before the change proceeds.
checklist.done: a dated production baseline export is attached to the ticket and reconciles to the last approved release, or drift is logged.

checklist.step: Rebuild the per-state SLA table from the regulatory source
actions: Export the 51 REG-027 jurisdiction rows from the Internal Regulatory System with the response window, day-count basis and citation.
Build the SLA table row per state with: response days, calendar/business/working-day basis, clock start (transmittal date vs receipt date), citation, verification date and verifier.

Set Alaska to 20 days from the Alaska Division of Insurance transmittal date, Arizona to 15 working days, California to 21 calendar days citing 10 CCR 2695.5(b), and complete every remaining state from its own source.
Add the rule that a due date printed on a DOI transmittal letter always overrides the table where it is earlier.
Hand the completed table to the Complaints Manager for review before it is coded.
checklist.done: all 51 SLA rows carry days, basis, clock start, citation and verification date, with the printed-date override rule stated and the table reviewed.

checklist.step: Configure the SLA clocks and the escalation ladder
actions: In the workflow/case management tool open Configuration ▸ Case Types ▸ Complaint ▸ SLA Definitions and load the state table, keying on forwarding state.
Set the clock to start on the DOI transmittal date field, not the case-created date, and attach the state holiday calendar to every business/working-day rule.
Configure the printed-due-date override so a value keyed from the transmittal letter supersedes the computed date and locks it against later editing.
Build the alert ladder: assignee at due −7, −3 and −1 days, Complaints Manager at −3 days, Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager on breach.
Configure the internal position-statement SLA at due date − 5 business days with escalation to the owning unit's manager.
checklist.done: SLA clocks compute from the transmittal date on the correct day basis with the printed-date override locked and the full alert ladder firing.

checklist.step: Enforce the mandatory register fields at the system level
actions: Make these fields mandatory to open a complaint case: DOI file number, forwarding state, transmittal date, date received, complainant name, policy or claim number, line of coverage.
Make these mandatory to close: function code, reason code, disposition, outcome, remedy amount where an outcome involves money, closure date, transmission proof attachment.
Block closure where no transmission proof document is attached and where the DOI response letter is missing from the case.
Set field-level validation so transmittal date cannot be later than date received and closure date cannot precede transmission date.
checklist.done: no complaint case can be opened or closed with a blank mandatory field, a missing transmission proof or an impossible date sequence.

checklist.step: Load the NAIC-aligned code lists under governance
actions: Load the function code list (underwriting, marketing & sales, policyholder service, claims) and the reason code list (denial of claim, delays, unsatisfactory settlement/offer, premium and rating, cancellation/nonrenewal, and the remaining NAIC reasons) as controlled pick lists.
Map every code to the corresponding Market Conduct Annual Statement complaint field so the annual submission derives from the register with no manual recoding.
Disable free-text entry on both fields and mark retired codes inactive rather than deleting them so historical cases keep their coding.
Record the code-list version and its owner on the change ticket.
checklist.done: function and reason codes are controlled pick lists mapped to MCAS fields, with free text disabled and retired codes preserved.

checklist.step: Bind the state correspondence templates to the case actions
actions: Bind the acknowledgment, DOI response and closing letter actions to the C01 controlled variants, keyed on the complainant's state and line of business.
Point the binding at the controlled library location so a retired edition can never be merged.
Configure the acknowledgment action to fire a task at case open with a 2-business-day due date.
Test one merge per template in the lower environment and confirm the correct state variant renders.
checklist.done: every letter action resolves to the current controlled variant for the case's state, with the acknowledgment task auto-created at open.

checklist.step: Write and run the regression test pack in the lower environment
actions: Write one test case per state that opens a complaint with a known transmittal date and asserts the computed due date matches the hand-computed date.
Add negative tests: blank mandatory field must block open, missing transmission proof must block closure, closure date before transmission date must be rejected, retired template must not merge.
Add boundary tests where the window crosses a weekend and a state holiday, and where the printed due date is earlier than the computed date.
Run the pack in the test environment, record pass/fail per case in the test plan and attach the results to the change ticket.
Re-run the full pack after every defect fix rather than testing the fix alone.
checklist.done: all 51 state date tests plus the negative and boundary tests pass, with results attached to the change ticket.

checklist.step: Prove the reporting extract still feeds the register and MCAS
actions: Run the complaint register extract from the test environment and confirm every mandatory field lands in the warehouse table with the right type and no truncation.
Reconcile the extract row count and the counts by state, function code and reason code to the case tool for the same test data set.
Confirm the MCAS-mapped fields populate for a full test year and that the aging buckets used by the daily dashboard still compute.
Attach the reconciliation to the change ticket.
checklist.done: the register extract reconciles row for row to the case tool with MCAS fields populated and aging buckets computing.

checklist.step: Take the change through the change advisory board
actions: Present the ticket with the baseline export, SLA table with citations, test results, warehouse reconciliation and back-out plan.
Obtain the Compliance Officer's approval on the SLA table specifically — IT approval alone is not sufficient for a regulatory timing rule.
Schedule the release window so it does not fall on a day with cases inside 2 days of their due date wherever avoidable.
Record the approvals, the implementer, the back-out owner and the validation owner on the ticket.
checklist.done: the change is approved by both the change advisory board and the Compliance Officer, with a scheduled window and named implementer, back-out and validation owners.

checklist.step: Deploy and validate in production before the window closes
actions: Deploy the configuration package to production in the approved window and export the post-change configuration immediately.
Diff the post-change export against the intended package and confirm nothing else moved.

Open three smoke-test complaint cases in production — one in a calendar-day state, one in a business-day state, one with a printed due date — and confirm the computed dates are right, then cancel them with a test marker.
Confirm the alert ladder fired on the smoke cases and that the acknowledgment task was created.
Where any smoke test fails, invoke the back-out plan inside the window rather than fixing forward.
checklist.done: the production export matches the intended package and the three smoke cases computed correct dates and fired their alerts, or the change was backed out.

checklist.step: Remediate cases already open under a superseded rule
actions: Where a state's window shortened, list every open case in that state and recompute its due date under the new rule.
Re-set the due dates on those cases and notify the assigned Complaints Specialists the same day with the new dates.
Where a case is already past the new due date, transmit what is available immediately and open a late-response exception under REG-027-C02.
Record the affected case count and the recovery actions on the change ticket.
checklist.done: every open case in a changed state has been recomputed and re-dated, with any resulting late case escalated and counted on the ticket.

checklist.step: Turn on continuous drift detection between the system and the source
actions: Schedule a monthly automated comparison of the production SLA table against the 51 REG-027 rows in the Internal Regulatory System.
Report any state where days, day basis, clock start or citation differ, and any state whose verification date is older than twelve months.
Route the drift report to the Business Systems Analyst and the Compliance Analyst with a 5-business-day resolution SLA.
Add a mandatory-field integrity check that flags any complaint closed in the month with a blank function code, reason code or missing transmission proof.
checklist.done: a monthly drift report runs against all 51 rows with a 5-business-day resolution SLA and a closed-case integrity check attached.

checklist.step: Attest the configuration quarterly
actions: Within 10 business days of quarter end, review the production configuration export against the approved baseline and the drift reports for the quarter.
Confirm every change in the quarter has an approved ticket and that no emergency change is unretrofitted with a normal ticket.
Sign the attestation naming the export reviewed, the exceptions found and their remediation status.
File the attestation and the export in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly attestation exists within 10 business days of quarter end, naming the export, exceptions and remediation status.

checklist.step: Retain the configuration record
actions: File the pre-change baseline, the SLA table with citations, test evidence, approvals, release record, post-change export and validation results under REG-027-C03 and the release date.
Apply a 7-year retention label so the configuration in force at any past date can be reconstructed for a market conduct exam.
Confirm the record is searchable by state, release date and change ticket number.
Have the Business Systems Analyst sign the release record as complete.
checklist.done: the release record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, searchable by state and ticket, and signed complete.

testing.step: Build the population of configuration rows and releases
actions: Export the current production complaint configuration: 51 SLA rows, mandatory field set, code lists, escalation rules and template bindings.
Extract every change ticket touching the complaint case type in the period, including emergency changes and standard changes.
Expect exactly 51 SLA rows — a missing or duplicated state row is an immediate exception.
Sign the extracts as complete with the extraction date and environment build number.
testing.done: a signed 51-row configuration export and a complete change-ticket list for the period are in hand.

testing.step: Reconcile production configuration to the approved baseline
actions: Diff the production export against the last approved release export attached to the change tickets.
List every difference and match it to an approved ticket; any difference with no ticket is unauthorised change.
Confirm every emergency change has a retrospective normal ticket approved within 5 business days.
Log unreconciled differences as exceptions rather than accepting a management explanation on its own.
testing.done: every production configuration difference is matched to an approved ticket or logged as unauthorised change.

testing.step: Draw the sample of states and releases
actions: Take 100% of states whose window changed in the period and 100% of business/working-day states, where the day-count basis carries the most error risk.
Add 15 remaining states by seeded random selection, and take 100% of emergency releases plus 3 randomly selected normal releases.
Record seed, population, strata and selection date in the workpaper.
Pull the SLA row, citation, test evidence and release record for each selected item.
testing.done: the sample covers changed and business-day states plus all emergency releases, and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the configured response window against the regulatory source
actions: For each sampled state read the underlying requirement yourself — the Alaska complaint-record requirement, the Arizona 15-working-day standard, California 10 CCR 2695.5(b), and the Alabama, Arkansas and Connecticut requirements — before opening the SLA row.
Reach your own conclusion on days, day-count basis and clock start, then compare to the configured row.
Treat a right number of days with the wrong basis or the wrong clock start as a fail, because it produces the wrong date.
Capture the source page you relied on, dated, into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independent conclusion on days, basis and clock start compared against the configured row, with a dated source capture.

testing.step: Recompute due dates in the live system with controlled test cases
actions: Open a marked test complaint in the production-equivalent environment for each sampled state with a transmittal date chosen to cross a weekend and a state holiday.
Read the due date the system computes and compare it to your hand computation using the state holiday calendar.
Run one case per sampled state with a printed transmittal due date earlier than the computed date and confirm the override applies and locks.
Record system date, hand date and pass/fail per state, and cancel the test cases with the test marker afterwards.
testing.done: system-computed and hand-computed due dates agree for every sampled state including holiday and override cases, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Test that the mandatory-field and closure blocks actually hold
actions: Attempt to open a complaint case with the DOI file number, transmittal date and line of coverage blank in turn and confirm each is blocked.
Attempt to close a case with a blank function code, a blank reason code and no transmission-proof attachment in turn and confirm each is blocked.
Attempt to key a closure date earlier than the transmission date and a transmittal date later than the receipt date and confirm both are rejected.
Attempt to enter free text into the reason-code field and confirm it is refused.
testing.done: every mandatory-field, closure and date-sequence block is proven to hold, with the attempts and system responses recorded.

testing.step: Trace the released configuration to its approvals and test evidence
actions: For each sampled release open the ticket and confirm the baseline export, test results, warehouse reconciliation and back-out plan are attached.
Confirm the Compliance Officer approved the SLA content specifically, not just the IT change, and that the approval pre-dates the deployment.
Confirm the post-deployment validation record exists with the three smoke cases and their computed dates.
Confirm segregation: the implementer is not the approver and is not the post-release validator.
testing.done: each sampled release has pre-dated compliance approval, attached test evidence, a validation record and proven segregation of duties.

testing.step: Test the register extract and MCAS mapping end to end
actions: Take 100 closed complaints from production and reconcile field by field to the warehouse register table: state, dates, function code, reason code, disposition, amount.
Recompute the transmittal-to-response day count in the warehouse and compare it to the case tool value for the same rows.
Trace the mapped MCAS complaint fields for a full data year and confirm the totals tie to the counts the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager reported.
List any field that truncates, defaults or nulls in transit.
testing.done: 100 sampled complaints reconcile field for field into the warehouse, day counts agree and MCAS-mapped totals tie to the reported figures.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the state or release, defect type (wrong window, wrong day basis, disabled mandatory field, unauthorised change, mapping defect) and the number of complaint cases handled under the defective rule.
Assign a root cause — source not re-read, holiday calendar not attached, emergency change unretrofitted, template rebind missed — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where cases were handled under a wrong window, hand the affected case list to the Complaints Manager for the C02 remediation path.
Flag every open exception for mandatory retest at the next release.
testing.done: every exception carries the state or release, defect type, affected case count, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest flag.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the SLA row defect count against the zero-tolerance threshold and the cosmetic drift rate against the 5% allowance.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references, and quantify complaint cases exposed to any defective rule.
Have a Compliance Officer who neither specified nor approved the sampled changes sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the IT Service Delivery Manager at the next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the defect count, exposed case volume, a conclusion and the reporting date, and is filed in the evidence repository.

In-scope processes.value: Annual training-needs analysis → curriculum refresh against regulatory change → assessment build → LMS assignment to complaint-touching roles → completion monitoring → delinquency escalation → attestation capture, covering Complaints, Consumer Affairs, contact centre, claims and underwriting staff who receive or answer complaints in any of the 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Course, assignment, completion and assessment records in the learning management system, with the in-scope audience derived from the HRIS position and org data

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every extension beyond the 31 May deadline and every decision to let an untrained employee keep handling complaints pending completion

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All employees and contingent workers holding a complaint-touching position at any point in the training year, per the HRIS position extract — including leavers, joiners and role transfers, not just the year-end headcount
