Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the completion test runs once after the 31 May deadline, with a quarterly joiner/transfer 30-day check between annual runs

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must have neither built, cleared nor administered the complaint-handling course

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual training compliance workpaper (HRIS population, LMS reconciliation, sampled completion records, content verification, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Course outline with its cited regulatory sources, the assignment and completion register by name and date, and sample assessment results — producible for a market conduct exam training request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager answers exam questions on training adequacy with the Compliance Manager supplying records; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement about untrained staff having handled complaints

checklist.step: Define the in-scope audience from the HRIS, not from a distribution list
actions: Export active positions from the HRIS and select every job code that receives, records, investigates or answers a complaint: Complaints Specialist, Consumer Affairs Analyst, Contact Center Agent and Supervisor, Claims Examiner and Adjuster, Policy Administration Analyst, Billing Specialist and their managers.
Add contingent workers and outsourced contact-centre staff with system access to the complaint case type, taken from the access review list.
Have each function head confirm their in-scope job codes in writing rather than assuming the job architecture is current.
Publish the audience rule as a saved HRIS query so the same definition drives assignment, monitoring and the audit population.
checklist.done: the audience is a saved HRIS query over confirmed job codes and includes contingent workers with complaint-system access.

checklist.step: Refresh the content against everything that changed this year
actions: Pull the REG-027 change log from the Internal Regulatory System for the last twelve months: response-window changes, register field changes and new notice wording from REG-027-C01.
Pull the prior year's complaint exceptions from the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager — late responses, miscoded reasons, missed acknowledgments — and turn the top causes into content.

Re-read the source text behind every window quoted in the course, including the Alaska complaint-record requirement, Arizona's 15 working days and California's 21 calendar days under 10 CCR 2695.5(b).
List the required content changes with their source citation and hand them to the Instructional Designer as the build brief.
checklist.done: a dated build brief lists every content change with its citation and the prior-year exception causes it addresses.

checklist.step: Build the course modules around what people actually get wrong
actions: Build five modules: recognising a complaint (including a verbal one), same-day logging and the mandatory register fields, computing the response due date, writing a response that answers every DOI question, and disposition coding.

Use a worked Alaska example end to end — an Alaska Division of Insurance transmittal, a 20-day due date computed from the transmittal date, the register fields keyed and the response elements assembled.
Contrast it with a business-day state and a state whose transmittal prints its own due date so learners see the override rule.
Include the REG-027-C01 notice block so staff recognise the text consumers are reading, and the escalation path for at-risk cases.
Keep each module under 20 minutes so it is completed rather than clicked through.
checklist.done: five modules exist with a worked Alaska example, a business-day contrast, the override rule and the escalation path, each under 20 minutes.

checklist.step: Build a scored assessment that tests judgement, not recall
actions: Write at least 20 questions, half of them scenario-based: given a transmittal letter image and a state, key the correct due date; given a consumer call transcript, decide whether it is a complaint.
Set the pass mark at 80% with a maximum of two retakes before manager involvement.
Randomise the question order and pull from a pool so consecutive learners do not share an answer key.
Have the Complaints Manager validate every scenario answer against how the case would actually be handled.
checklist.done: a randomised 20-question assessment with an 80% pass mark exists, with scenario answers validated by the Complaints Manager.

checklist.step: Clear the course content with Compliance and Counsel before release
actions: Review every regulatory statement in the course against the citation on the build brief.
Route to Regulatory Counsel any module that states a legal obligation or a consumer right, and record counsel's clearance date.
Reject any slide stating a response window with no cited source, and any that quotes a superseded window.
Version the course as REG-027-C04-<year>-v<n> and record the clearance in the course properties.
checklist.done: every regulatory statement traces to a cited source and the course version carries a dated compliance and counsel clearance.

checklist.step: Load the course and its completion rules into the LMS
actions: Load the SCORM package into the learning management system, set the assessment pass mark to 80% and the retake limit to two.
Set the completion rule so a learner is complete only on a passed assessment, not on module views.
Configure the certificate and the completion record to capture learner name, employee id, job code, completion date and score.
Run a pilot with five Complaints Specialists and fix any tracking or scoring defect before general release.
checklist.done: the course is live with an 80% pass-gated completion rule, a full completion record schema and a clean five-learner pilot.

checklist.step: Assign the course against the HRIS audience with the right due dates
actions: Assign the course by 1 March to every worker returned by the saved HRIS audience query, with a 31 May due date.
Build the dynamic rule so any HRIS record entering an in-scope job code is auto-assigned with a due date 30 days from the start or transfer date.
Assign contingent workers through their manager of record so nobody with complaint-system access is unassigned.
Reconcile the assignment count to the HRIS audience count on release day and resolve any difference the same week.
checklist.done: every worker in the HRIS audience holds an assignment with the correct due date, and assignment count reconciles to headcount.

checklist.step: Launch with communications that name the deadline and the consequence
actions: Send the launch note from the Head of Compliance naming the 31 May deadline, the 80% pass mark and what happens on non-completion.
Give people managers a roster of their in-scope staff and their due dates so completion is a line-management task, not an LMS task.
Brief the Contact Center Ops Manager and Claims Director / Manager to build course time into the shift and workload plan.
Post the course link and the FAQ where staff already work rather than only in the LMS catalogue.
checklist.done: staff and managers have a dated launch note with the deadline, pass mark and consequence, and managers hold their own rosters.

checklist.step: Monitor completion weekly and publish it by team
actions: Build a weekly completion dashboard from the LMS extract showing percentage complete by function, team and manager, with a named not-yet-complete list.
Publish it every Monday to function heads from 1 April so the gap is visible eight weeks before the deadline.
Track first-attempt pass rate and flag any module where the failure rate exceeds 20% for content rework.
Reconcile the dashboard population to the HRIS audience monthly so joiners appear without manual intervention.
checklist.done: a weekly by-team completion dashboard runs from 1 April with named outstanding learners and a monthly HRIS reconciliation.

checklist.step: Escalate delinquency on a fixed ladder
actions: At 1 June send every incomplete learner and their line manager a named notice with a 10-business-day recovery date.
At 15 June escalate the remaining names to the function head, and at 30 June to the Head of Compliance and the HR Business Partner.
For anyone still incomplete, decide with the Complaints Manager whether complaint-queue access is suspended until completion, and record the decision.
Log every delinquency with the name, job code, days overdue, escalation stage and the access decision.
checklist.done: every incomplete learner has passed through the dated escalation ladder with a recorded access decision and a logged delinquency.

checklist.step: Run the 30-day joiner and transfer cycle continuously
actions: Include the complaint-handling course in the onboarding checklist for every in-scope job code so it is assigned on day one.
Run a monthly report of HRIS starters and transfers into in-scope job codes and reconcile it to the LMS auto-assignments.
Flag any joiner who reached day 25 without completion to their manager, and day 31 to the Compliance Manager.
Confirm leavers are removed from the assignment population so the completion rate is not distorted.
checklist.done: every in-scope joiner and transfer is assigned on day one, chased at day 25 and escalated at day 31, with leavers removed.

checklist.step: Capture the individual attestation with the completion
actions: Present an attestation at the end of the assessment: the learner confirms they will log every complaint the day it is received, key the mandatory register fields and escalate any case at risk of its due date.
Store the attestation text version, the learner id and the timestamp with the completion record.
Require re-attestation on the annual course rather than carrying the prior year's forward.
Confirm the attestation record exports with the completion extract for audit.
checklist.done: every completion carries a timestamped attestation of the current year's wording, exportable with the completion record.

checklist.step: Measure whether the training actually changed handling
actions: Compare the complaint QA scores, late-response count and miscoding rate for the six months after the course to the six months before, by team.
Cross-reference teams with a high assessment failure rate against teams with a high complaint exception rate.
Where a team shows no improvement, commission targeted coaching from the Trainer rather than re-issuing the same e-learning.
Feed the findings into next year's build brief.
checklist.done: a before-and-after comparison of late responses, QA scores and miscoding by team exists, with targeted coaching commissioned where flat.

checklist.step: Report training status to the Compliance Committee
actions: Report each quarter: assigned, complete, overdue and access-suspended counts by function, plus joiner 30-day compliance.
Name any function below 100% at the reporting date and the recovery commitment its head has given.
Record the committee's decisions and any deadline extension granted in the minutes and on the exception log.
Confirm the annual figure is available for the market conduct exam response pack.
checklist.done: quarterly committee minutes record completion by function, named laggards, recovery commitments and any granted extension.

checklist.step: Retain the training record for the exam look-back period
actions: File the course version and its content sources, the assignment list, the per-learner completion and score records, attestations and escalation log under REG-027-C04 and the training year.
Apply a 5-year retention label so the record covers the usual market conduct exam look-back.
Confirm the record is searchable by employee name, job code, completion date and course version.
Have the Compliance Manager sign the year's record as complete.
checklist.done: the training year's record is filed, labelled for 5-year retention, searchable by name and job code, and signed complete.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope workers for the whole year
actions: Extract from the HRIS every worker who held an in-scope job code at any point in the training year, with start, transfer and leave dates.
Add contingent workers and outsourced contact-centre staff from the complaint case-type access list in the identity platform.
Do not use the year-end headcount — mid-year joiners and leavers are exactly where training gaps sit.
Sign the extract as complete with the extraction date and the job-code list used.
testing.done: the population covers every in-scope worker at any point in the year including contingent staff, and the extract is signed.

testing.step: Reconcile the HRIS population to the LMS assignment register
actions: Match every population row to an LMS assignment on employee id.
List workers with no assignment and assignments with no matching in-scope worker, and clear each with the Learning Development Manager.
Compare the audience rule used for assignment against the job-code list you built; a narrower rule is itself a finding.
Treat any in-scope worker never assigned as an automatic exception regardless of whether they handled a complaint.
testing.done: every in-scope worker is matched to an assignment or logged as an unassigned exception, with the audience rule compared.

testing.step: Draw the sample of learners and records
actions: Take 100% of mid-year joiners and transfers into in-scope roles and 100% of workers recorded as incomplete or extended.
Add 25 completed learners by seeded random selection across functions, minimum 40 records in total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Pull the completion record, score, attestation and the assignment history for each sampled learner.
testing.done: the sample covers all joiners, transfers and incompletes plus a reproducible random selection of completions, with records in hand.

testing.step: Re-perform completion and score verification in the LMS
actions: Open each sampled learner's transcript in the LMS and read the completion date, score, attempt count and course version directly.
Confirm the score meets the 80% pass mark and that completion was gated on the passed assessment rather than module views.
Confirm the course version completed is the current training year's version, not a carried-forward prior-year record.
Compare each transcript value to the completion register export and list any difference.
testing.done: each sampled completion is verified in the LMS for date, score, attempts and course version, with register differences listed.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths for every sampled learner
actions: For existing staff, compare the completion date to the 31 May deadline and compute days late.
For joiners and transfers, recompute the due date as start or transfer date plus 30 days from the HRIS record and compare to the completion date.
Confirm any completion after the deadline carries a Head of Compliance extension approval that pre-dates the deadline.
Treat a post-deadline completion with no pre-dated approval as a fail against the 100% threshold.
testing.done: days-late is computed for every sampled learner against the correct deadline, with extensions traced to pre-dated approvals.

testing.step: Verify the course content against the regulatory text yourself
actions: Take every response window, register field and consumer-notice statement asserted in the course and check it against the current source.
Confirm the Alaska worked example computes 20 days from the Alaska Division of Insurance transmittal date and that the Arizona 15-working-day and California 21-calendar-day statements are current.
Confirm the course reflects the current REG-027-C01 notice wording and the current mandatory register fields configured under REG-027-C03.
Treat a course teaching a superseded window as a content fail, not a documentation gap, and quantify how many learners completed that version.
testing.done: every regulatory statement in the course is verified against current source text, with superseded content and its completion volume quantified.

testing.step: Test whether untrained staff actually handled complaints
actions: Extract the handler id from every complaint case worked during the year in the workflow/case management tool.
Join the handler list to the LMS completion register and list every handler with no passed completion at the date they worked the case.
For each such handler, pull the cases they touched and the dates, and confirm whether any went overdue or was miscoded.
Treat any complaint handled without a recorded pass as a fail, with the case list attached.
testing.done: every complaint handler is matched to a completion valid at the handling date, with untrained-handler cases listed.

testing.step: Test the attestation and escalation records
actions: Confirm each sampled completion carries a timestamped attestation using the current year's wording.
For sampled incomplete learners, trace the 1 June, 15 June and 30 June escalations and the recorded access decision.
Confirm anyone whose complaint-queue access was to be suspended actually lost access on the recorded date, by checking the identity platform entitlement history.
List any escalation stage skipped or access decision recorded but not enacted.
testing.done: attestations, dated escalations and enacted access decisions are verified for every sampled learner, with gaps listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the worker, job code, function, defect type (unassigned, late, failed and not retaken, untrained handler, stale content) and days overdue.
Assign a root cause — audience rule missed the job code, onboarding checklist omitted the course, manager not chased, content not refreshed — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for untrained handlers, require completion within 10 business days and a QA review of their handled cases.
Flag every open exception for mandatory retest in the quarterly joiner check.
testing.done: every exception carries the worker, defect type, days overdue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest flag.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the completion rate against the 100% threshold, the joiner 30-day rate, and the count of complaints handled by untrained staff.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references and the exception list by function.
Have a reviewer who neither built nor administered the course sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states completion rates, untrained-handler volume, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, and is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the complaint register as the market-conduct record of truth, the root-cause programme behind it and the complaint figures reported to the NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement; escalates systemic drivers to the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the register schema and monitoring scope are re-verified against the current complaint-record provisions each year: the Alaska complaint-record requirement (rep) with its market-conduct tracking expectation, plus the Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California and Connecticut complaint-record requirements, and the NAIC Market Conduct Examiners Handbook complaint-register field expectations

In-scope processes.value: Daily complaint intake reconciliation → aging and disposition monitoring → root-cause coding → trend and complaint-index analysis → remediation and restitution → MCAS complaint reconciliation → committee and DOI market-analysis reporting, across all DOI-forwarded and directly received complaints in the 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: The complaint register in the workflow/case management tool as system of record, its warehouse extract for trending and the NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement submission derived from it; NAIC Consumer Information Source used for external benchmarking

Compliance procedure documented.value: Complaint Monitoring & Root Cause Procedure — daily reconciliation, weekly aging review, root-cause taxonomy, thematic threshold rules, remediation and restitution protocol, MCAS reconciliation, escalation to the Compliance Committee

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and noted by the Compliance Committee; re-approved annually and whenever the NAIC reason-code set or the MCAS complaint definitions change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous — daily intake reconciliation, weekly aging review, monthly root-cause pack, quarterly Compliance Committee report; the NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement complaint data is due 30 April for the prior data year, with the register frozen and reconciled by 31 March

Deadline reminders configured.value: Daily 09:00 reconciliation task, Monday aging-review task, month-end root-cause pack task, and MCAS milestones at 31 January (data cut), 28 February (coding cleanse) and 31 March (frozen register sign-off) ahead of the 30 April submission

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Register extracts, daily reconciliations, root-cause analyses, remediation and restitution records, MCAS reconciliations and committee packs retained 5 years — the market conduct exam look-back — with the frozen annual register kept immutably

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Complaints missing from the register, root causes left uncoded past 10 business days, remediation actions past due and any theme breaching its threshold without an opened action are logged with owner and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every systemic root-cause finding, every restitution population and every decision not to remediate a theme that breached its threshold

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All complaints on the register for the test period across the 51 jurisdictions — DOI-forwarded and direct — plus the root-cause codes, remediation actions and the MCAS complaint counts derived from them

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a DOI-forwarded complaint absent from the register or on an MCAS complaint count that does not tie to the frozen register; root-cause coding accuracy must be ≥95% on re-performance; any theme above 10 complaints in a rolling quarter without an opened remediation action is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; monitoring effectiveness is tested quarterly over that quarter's register, with an additional pre-submission test on the frozen annual register before the 30 April MCAS filing

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must have coded none of the sampled complaints and own none of the sampled themes or remediation actions

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly complaint monitoring workpaper and the annual MCAS pre-submission reconciliation (register extract, DOI reconciliation, coding re-performance, theme analysis, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Complaint register export by state, function and reason code with disposition and cycle times, the root-cause pack and remediation status — the standard opening request in a market conduct exam, producible within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns DOI market-analysis inquiries and exam complaint requests; Regulatory Counsel clears any submission conceding a systemic practice issue or committing to restitution

checklist.step: Reconcile the day's intake against every inbound channel
actions: Every business morning list new cases opened in the workflow/case management tool since the previous run.

Compare against the NAIC State Based Systems complaint module inbox, the state DOI portals, the complaints mailbox, the executive-office escalation queue and the contact centre's complaint-tagged interactions.
Open a case the same day for anything present in a channel but absent from the register, and record why it was missed.
Record the reconciliation result — channel counts, register count, differences and resolution — as a dated daily record.
checklist.done: a dated daily reconciliation shows channel counts equal to register counts, with any difference opened as a case the same day.

checklist.step: Work the aging and disposition review every Monday
actions: Open the complaint aging dashboard and review open cases by days-to-due, by state and by owning function.
Review cases open beyond 30 days regardless of due date, and every case reopened by a DOI, with the assigned specialist.
Read the previous week's closures for coding completeness before they leave the review — blanks are cheaper to fix now than at MCAS freeze.
Record attendance, decisions and the named owner for each at-risk case in the meeting note.
checklist.done: a weekly note records the aging position, at-risk cases with named owners and the coding-completeness check on the week's closures.

checklist.step: Code a root cause on every closed complaint within 10 business days
actions: Read the complaint file and assign a root cause from the controlled taxonomy: policy language unclear, rating or billing error, claim decision error, service delay, agent conduct, system defect, or no company error.
Name the specific driver — the form provision, rating rule, letter template, workflow step or job aid at fault — not just the category.
Attribute the cause to an owning function and, where a system defect, raise the ticket with the Business Systems Analyst and link it.
Distinguish root cause from disposition: a complaint can be upheld for the consumer with no company error, and vice versa.
Escalate to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager any cause implicating a filed form or a rating rule.
checklist.done: every complaint closed in the period carries a taxonomy root cause, a named specific driver and an owning function within 10 business days.

checklist.step: Run the monthly theme analysis over the register
actions: Pull the register extract and count complaints by reason code, function code, state, product, distribution channel and root-cause driver for the rolling quarter.
Apply the thresholds: any driver above 10 complaints in a rolling quarter, or any state whose complaint count doubles month on month, opens a theme.
Normalise by exposure — complaints per 10,000 policies in force and per 1,000 claims closed — so a large state does not mask a small one with a real problem.
Write each theme up with its count, trend, affected population and the evidence behind it.
checklist.done: the monthly pack lists every threshold-breaching theme with counts, exposure-normalised rates, trend and affected population.

checklist.step: Benchmark against the published external picture
actions: Pull the company's NAIC Consumer Information Source complaint index and closed-complaint counts by line and compare to the peer median.
Compare the NAIC-published reason-code mix to the internal register mix; a mismatch usually means internal coding is drifting.
Compare complaints per 10,000 policies in force by state against the prior two years to spot a state trending out of line.
Take any index above 1.00 for a line into the theme list with a named owner.
checklist.done: the external complaint index and reason mix are compared to internal data, with every above-median line taken into the theme list.

checklist.step: Open a remediation action for every theme that breaches
actions: Raise an action in the GRC platform per theme with the driver, affected states, complaint count, owning function head and a target date.

Specify the fix type: form wording change routed to REG-027-C01, rating or rule change, letter template change, workflow reconfiguration routed to REG-027-C03, training routed to REG-027-C04, or agent conduct action.
Require the owner to state the affected consumer population, not just the complainants, so silent detriment is addressed.
Where no action is opened, record the Head of Compliance's written rationale on the theme.
checklist.done: every breaching theme carries an owned, dated remediation action with a fix type and affected population, or a signed rationale for no action.

checklist.step: Decide and execute restitution where consumers were out of pocket
actions: Where the root cause caused financial detriment, ask the owning function for the full affected population, not only those who complained.
Compute the redress per consumer including any statutory interest the state requires on delayed claim or premium refunds, and total it.
Route the population and the computation to Regulatory Counsel and the Head of Compliance for approval before any payment.
Hand the approved payment file to Billing or Claims, track it to completion and reconcile paid records back to the approved population.
Record the restitution on the theme so it can be produced in a market conduct exam.
checklist.done: each detriment theme has an approved affected population, a computed redress with interest, an executed payment file and a paid-to-approved reconciliation.

checklist.step: Detect repeat and linked complaints before a regulator does
actions: Run a monthly match on policy number, complainant name and household to find consumers complaining more than once in twelve months.
Run a match on producer code and on handler id to find complaint clusters attaching to one agent or one adjuster.
Escalate producer clusters to the Producer Compliance Manager and handler clusters to the owning function head with the case list.
Treat a repeat complaint on the same issue as evidence the first remediation failed, and reopen the theme rather than the case alone.
checklist.done: repeat complainants and producer/handler clusters are identified monthly and escalated with their case lists.

checklist.step: Track remediation actions to closure with evidence
actions: Review open actions monthly and record the percentage complete, the blocker and the revised date where slipped.
Require closure evidence — the released form edition, the change ticket, the training completion figure, the payment reconciliation — before an action may be closed.
Escalate any action past due by 30 days to the Head of Compliance with the reason.
Re-measure the complaint count for the driver 90 days after closure and reopen the action where the count has not fallen.
checklist.done: every action closes on attached evidence and is re-measured 90 days later, with slipped actions escalated at 30 days past due.

checklist.step: Freeze and reconcile the register for the MCAS submission
actions: Cut the data-year register at 31 January and circulate the blanks and miscoding list to the Complaints Manager for cleanse by 28 February.
Reconcile the register complaint counts by line of business and state to the NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement complaint fields, and to the counts the DOIs themselves forwarded.
Freeze the register at 31 March, take an immutable extract and have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager sign it.
Submit the MCAS complaint data by the 30 April deadline and file the submission confirmation with the frozen extract.
Investigate and document any difference between the company count and the NAIC-published count for the same year.
checklist.done: the register is cleansed, reconciled to MCAS fields and to DOI-forwarded counts, frozen and signed by 31 March, and submitted by 30 April.

checklist.step: Stand ready for DOI market-analysis inquiries
actions: Keep a standing exam pack refreshed quarterly: register export by state, reason and function code, cycle-time statistics, the root-cause pack and open remediation status.
Test quarterly that the pack can be produced within 5 business days by actually producing it from the current data.
On receiving a market-analysis inquiry, log it, name a single owner and answer strictly to the question asked, with Regulatory Counsel clearing anything conceding a practice issue.
Record the inquiry, response and outcome on the regulatory interaction log.
checklist.done: a refreshed exam pack exists, its 5-business-day producibility is proven quarterly, and every DOI inquiry is logged with an owner and a cleared response.

checklist.step: Report the complaint picture to the Compliance Committee
actions: Present quarterly: volumes and rates by state and line, top reason codes, top root-cause drivers, late-response count, open themes and remediation status, and the external complaint index.
Name every theme older than two quarters without closure and the owner accountable.
Take committee decisions on anything requiring investment or a product change and record them in the minutes.
Escalate to the Board risk committee any theme with regulatory-action or restitution exposure above the agreed threshold.
checklist.done: quarterly minutes record volumes, drivers, open themes with named owners, restitution exposure and any board escalation.

checklist.step: Keep the taxonomy and the monitoring rules current
actions: Review the root-cause taxonomy annually against the year's 'other' codings; where 'other' exceeds 10% of closures, add the missing categories.
Re-check the reason and function code lists against the current NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement definitions and route any change to REG-027-C03 for configuration.
Re-set the theme thresholds against actual volumes so they neither fire constantly nor never fire.
Record the review, the changes and the approval on the procedure document.
checklist.done: the taxonomy, code lists and thresholds are reviewed annually with 'other' coding below 10% and changes routed to configuration.

checklist.step: Feed the findings back into forms, systems and training
actions: Send the Policy Forms Specialist every theme naming a form provision or notice wording as a C01 change driver.
Send the Business Systems Analyst every theme naming a workflow or SLA defect as a C03 change driver.
Send the Instructional Designer the year's top five drivers as the C04 build brief input.
Confirm each recipient has raised the corresponding change record and record the reference on the theme.
checklist.done: every theme naming a form, system or knowledge driver has a corresponding C01, C03 or C04 change record referenced back on it.

checklist.step: Retain the monitoring record for the exam look-back
actions: File daily reconciliations, weekly aging notes, monthly root-cause packs, theme records, restitution reconciliations, frozen MCAS extracts and committee packs under REG-027-C05 by period.
Apply a 5-year retention label and hold the frozen annual register immutably so a prior-year MCAS figure can always be reproduced.
Confirm the record is searchable by state, reason code, root-cause driver, theme id and period.
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager sign each period as complete.
checklist.done: the monitoring record is filed by period, labelled for 5-year retention, immutable for frozen registers, searchable and signed complete.

testing.step: Build the complaint population for the test period
actions: Extract every complaint on the register with a received date in the period, with state, channel, line of business, function and reason codes, disposition, root cause and cycle times.
Split DOI-forwarded from directly received complaints — the record obligation bites hardest on the DOI-forwarded set.
Record the extract query, date and row count and sign the extract as complete.
Do not accept a pre-built management report as the population.
testing.done: a signed, query-documented register extract for the period exists, split by DOI-forwarded and direct.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to what the regulators and channels actually produced
actions: Pull the inbound lists from the NAIC State Based Systems complaint module and each state DOI portal for the period and match on DOI file number.
Sweep the complaints mailbox, the executive escalation queue and the contact centre's complaint-tagged interactions for items with no register entry.
Compare the company's NAIC Consumer Information Source published closed-complaint count for the year to the register count and explain the difference.
Treat every DOI-forwarded complaint absent from the register as an automatic fail against the zero-tolerance threshold.
testing.done: every DOI transmittal and channel item is matched to a register row or logged as a missing-complaint fail, with the NAIC published count explained.

testing.step: Draw the sample across states, reasons and root causes
actions: Take 100% of complaints coded to a systemic theme, 100% coded root cause 'other', and 100% with a restitution payment.
Add 30 by seeded random selection stratified across the five highest-volume states and the four function codes, minimum 45 in total.
Record the seed, strata, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
Pull the full complaint file and the coding history for each sampled case.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers themed, 'other'-coded and restitution cases, and each file is in hand.

testing.step: Re-perform the coding on the sample without looking at the register
actions: Read each sampled complaint file and assign your own function code, reason code and root cause before opening the register row.
Compare and compute the agreement rate against the 95% accuracy threshold, separately for reason code and root cause.
Flag any case coded 'no company error' where the file shows a company error, and any coded 'other' where a taxonomy category clearly fits.
Record each disagreement with the file evidence that drove your conclusion.
testing.done: an independent re-coding exists for every sampled case with an agreement rate computed against the 95% threshold and disagreements evidenced.

testing.step: Re-run the theme analysis independently from raw data
actions: Recompute complaint counts by reason code, root-cause driver and state over the rolling quarter directly from the register table.
Recompute the exposure-normalised rates — complaints per 10,000 policies in force and per 1,000 claims closed — using policy and claim counts from source, not from the monitoring pack.
Apply the documented thresholds yourself and list every theme that should have opened.
Compare your list to the themes management actually opened; an unopened breaching theme is a fail.
testing.done: themes are independently recomputed from raw data and compared to those opened, with unopened breaches listed as fails.

testing.step: Test that remediation actions were real and effective
actions: For each open and closed theme, open the GRC action and confirm the owner, target date and fix type are recorded.

For closed actions, open the claimed closure evidence — the released form edition, the change ticket, the training completion figure, the payment reconciliation — and confirm it exists and matches the claim.
Recompute the 90-day post-closure complaint count for the driver and confirm it fell; where it did not, confirm the action was reopened.
Treat an action closed on an assertion with no attached evidence as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled action's closure evidence is inspected and its 90-day re-measurement recomputed, with evidence-free closures failed.

testing.step: Verify restitution reached the whole affected population
actions: For each restitution theme, take the approved affected population and reconcile it to the payment records in the billing and claims payment systems.
Recompute the per-consumer redress including any statutory interest the state required, on a sample of 20 payees.
Confirm the population was drawn on the root-cause criteria, not limited to consumers who complained.
List unpaid, underpaid or excluded consumers with the amounts involved.
testing.done: approved restitution populations reconcile to executed payments, redress is recomputed on 20 payees, and shortfalls are quantified.

testing.step: Reconcile the MCAS complaint figures to the frozen register
actions: Take the submitted Market Conduct Annual Statement complaint counts by line and state and tie them to the frozen 31 March register extract.
Confirm the frozen extract carries the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager's signature and pre-dates the 30 April submission.
Recompute any derived figure — complaints per policy, average days to close — from the frozen extract and compare to what was filed.
Treat any unexplained difference between filed and register figures as a fail against the zero-tolerance threshold.
testing.done: filed MCAS complaint counts tie to a signed, pre-dated frozen register with derived figures recomputed, or the difference is failed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the case or theme id, state, defect type (missing complaint, miscoding, unopened theme, evidence-free closure, restitution shortfall, MCAS difference) and the consumer volume affected.
Assign a root cause — channel not swept, taxonomy gap, threshold not applied, action closed on assertion, cleanse missed the blanks — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for missing complaints and MCAS differences, decide with Regulatory Counsel whether a correction to the forwarding DOI or a refiling is required.
Flag every open exception for mandatory retest next quarter.
testing.done: every exception carries a case or theme id, defect type, affected volume, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest flag.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the missing-complaint count, the coding agreement rate against 95%, the unopened-theme count and the MCAS tie result.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references and the themes driving it.
Have a reviewer who neither coded nor owned any sampled complaint or theme sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.

Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting, escalate restitution exposure to the Board risk committee where it breaches the threshold, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the missing-complaint count, coding accuracy, unopened themes, the MCAS tie result, a conclusion and the reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual independent audit of complaint notice content and response timing, its scope across the 51 jurisdictions and the issued audit report; escalates unaccepted management action plans to the Audit Committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the audit criteria matrix is rebuilt from current text at planning: the Alaska complaint-record requirement (rep) and the Alaska Division of Insurance 20-day response practice, Arizona's 15 working days, California 10 CCR 2695.5(b) 21 calendar days, plus the Alabama, Arkansas and Connecticut complaint-record requirements, with each criterion carrying its source and verification date

In-scope processes.value: Annual audit lifecycle over REG-027 — planning and risk assessment, criteria matrix build, walkthroughs of C01 to C05, population extraction, statistical sampling, content and timing testing, exception validation, reporting, management action plan agreement and follow-up to closure, across all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Audit plan, workpapers, samples, issues and management action plans in the audit platform, drawing populations from the workflow/case management tool, the document management repository and the form inventory in the policy administration platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: REG-027 Complaint Notice & Timing Audit Programme — scope, criteria matrix schema, sampling methodology and confidence level, content and timing test steps, exception validation protocol, reporting standard and follow-up cadence

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Audit Executive and accepted by the Audit Committee in the annual plan; the audit programme is re-approved before each year's fieldwork

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — planning memo issued by 31 January, fieldwork closed by 31 March, draft report to management within 10 business days of fieldwork close, management responses within 15 business days, final report issued to the Audit Committee within 30 business days of fieldwork close, and follow-up testing 90 days after each action's due date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Audit platform milestone alerts on the planning memo, fieldwork close, draft issue, management response and final issue dates, plus automatic follow-up tasks 90 days after every management action due date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Planning memo, criteria matrix with citations, walkthrough notes, population extracts, sampling documentation, per-sample test evidence, exception validation, report and action-plan closure evidence retained 7 years as the audit file

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every content or timing failure is raised as a rated audit issue with the criterion breached, the affected population, the agreed action, the owner and the due date, and is tracked to evidenced closure

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the final report, approves every issue rating and closes each management action only on inspected evidence and successful follow-up testing

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: For content: every live complaint-notice artifact by jurisdiction and artifact type. For timing: every DOI-forwarded complaint closed in the audit year. Both drawn independently of management's own extracts

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Timing: any response transmitted after its governing due date without a pre-dated written extension is an exception; more than 2% of the timing sample late rates the issue High. Content: any missing notice or wrong DOI contact block rates High regardless of rate; formatting-only defects rate Low below 5%

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The underlying obligation is event-driven and continuous; independent audit runs annually over the full year, with 90-day follow-up testing on every open action between annual cycles

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: An external quality assessor or an auditor from another engagement who performed none of the sampled REG-027 audit testing

Evidence location for test results.value: The REG-027 annual audit file in the audit platform — planning memo, criteria matrix, populations, sampling documentation, test workpapers, exception schedules, report and follow-up evidence — cross-referenced from the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The issued audit report with its scope, criteria, sample sizes, exception counts and management action plans, plus follow-up closure evidence — routinely requested at the opening of a market conduct exam and producible within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Audit Executive releases audit reports to a regulator only through the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with Regulatory Counsel's clearance, and never rewrites a finding to soften an exam position

checklist.step: Scope the audit and issue the planning memo by 31 January
actions: Set the scope: complaint notice content on consumer documents and DOI response timing across all 51 jurisdictions for the prior calendar year, covering C01 through C05.
Set the risk basis from the prior year — late-response counts by state, DOI market-analysis inquiries, exam criticisms and open C05 themes — and name the higher-risk states for full coverage.
Name the engagement lead, the team, the auditee contacts (Policy Forms Specialist, Complaints Manager, Business Systems Analyst, Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager) and the milestone dates.
Issue the planning memo to the auditees and the Audit Committee chair by 31 January and log it in the audit platform.
checklist.done: a planning memo naming scope, risk basis, team, auditee contacts and milestone dates is issued by 31 January.

checklist.step: Build the audit criteria matrix from primary regulatory text
actions: Build one criteria row per jurisdiction: required notice content and placement, required DOI contact block, response window in days, day-count basis and clock start, with the citation and the date you read it.

Read the primary source yourself for every criterion — the Alaska complaint-record requirement, Arizona's 15 working days, California 10 CCR 2695.5(b), and the Alabama, Arkansas and Connecticut requirements — and do not inherit management's REG-027-C03 SLA table.
Capture each source page to the audit file, dated, as the criterion's support.
Have a second auditor review the matrix for completeness against the 51-jurisdiction scope before testing starts.
checklist.done: all 51 criteria rows carry independently sourced content and timing criteria with dated captures and a second-auditor review.

checklist.step: Walk through the notice build and the response process end to end
actions: Walk one notice change with the Policy Forms Specialist from intake to published edition, observing the matrix, counsel clearance and template binding in the systems themselves.
Walk one complaint with a Complaints Specialist from transmittal intake to closure, watching the due date compute and the transmission proof attach live.
Walk the configuration path with the Business Systems Analyst and the monitoring path with the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
Write the walkthrough notes naming the controls observed, the evidence each produces and the points where the process depends on a person remembering.
checklist.done: four dated walkthrough notes exist naming observed controls, their evidence and the manual dependencies identified.

checklist.step: Extract the timing population independently of management
actions: Run your own query against the complaint case data for every DOI-forwarded complaint with a transmittal date in the audit year, capturing transmittal date, printed due date, transmission date, state and disposition.
Reconcile your row count to the NAIC State Based Systems and state portal inbound lists for the year and to the register count management reported.
Investigate and document every difference before sampling; a population that only ties to management's own extract has not been independently established.
Sign the population as complete with the query, run date and row count recorded.
checklist.done: an independently queried timing population is reconciled to regulator inbound lists and management's register, with differences documented.

checklist.step: Extract the content population from live artifacts
actions: Pull the live correspondence templates and form editions tagged with the complaint notice from the policy administration platform and the controlled library.

Independently pull real issued documents from the document archive — policy jackets, acknowledgments and denial letters — for every jurisdiction, so the test hits what consumers received rather than what was configured.
Build the population grid of 51 jurisdictions by artifact type and flag any empty cell before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction date and method.
checklist.done: a signed content population covers every jurisdiction/artifact cell using real issued documents, with empty cells flagged.

checklist.step: Set and document the sampling plan
actions: Set the statistical basis: 90% confidence with a 5% tolerable deviation rate for the timing sample, and state the resulting sample size.
Take 100% of the higher-risk states named in the planning memo, 100% of complaints that management recorded as late or extended, and 100% of jurisdictions with prescribed verbatim notice wording.
Draw the remainder with a seeded random selection and record the seed, tool, strata and draw date.
Have the engagement lead approve the plan before selection so sample size is not adjusted after results are seen.
checklist.done: an approved, statistically stated sampling plan is documented with seed, strata and full coverage of risk-flagged items.

checklist.step: Test the notice content on the sampled issued documents
actions: Compare the printed notice block on each sampled issued document to the criteria row: wording verbatim where prescribed, correct DOI address, phone and URL, correct placement and prominence.
Confirm the block appears on every artifact type the criterion requires, not only the policy jacket.
Open the printed URL and dial the printed number on a subsample of at least ten jurisdictions and record the result.
Attach the annotated document image to the workpaper for each sampled item.
checklist.done: each sampled document is scored against its criteria row with annotated images and live URL/phone checks recorded.

checklist.step: Test response timing against your own recomputed due dates
actions: Read the due date from the transmittal letter image rather than from the case field; where none is printed, recompute from the criteria row using the correct day basis and state holiday calendar.
Read the transmission timestamp from the portal confirmation or sent-email header rather than from the case field, and compute days early or late.
Where an extension is claimed, confirm a written DOI grant exists and pre-dates the original due date.
Record source date, computed date, actual date and result on the timing workpaper for every sampled complaint.
checklist.done: every sampled complaint has a recomputed due date, a proof-based transmission date and a days early/late result on the workpaper.

checklist.step: Test the completeness of the complaint record itself
actions: For each sampled complaint confirm the file holds the transmittal, acknowledgment, position statement, cleared response, enclosures, transmission proof and disposition coding.
Confirm the register row carries state, dates, function code, reason code, disposition and outcome with no blanks — these are the fields a market conduct examiner pulls first.
Confirm the file is retrievable by DOI file number and that its retention label is set to 5 years from closure.
Treat a timely response with an incomplete record as a record-keeping exception in its own right.
checklist.done: every sampled complaint file is scored for the required documents, register fields and retention label, with gaps listed separately from timing results.

checklist.step: Validate every exception with the process owner before it becomes an issue
actions: Send each provisional exception to the Complaints Manager or Policy Forms Specialist with the evidence attached and a 3-business-day response window.
Accept a withdrawal only where new evidence is produced — a written DOI extension, a different transmission proof — and file that evidence in the workpaper.
Record every disputed exception with both positions and let the engagement lead rule.
Do not soften an exception because management explains why it happened; explanation is root cause, not withdrawal.
checklist.done: every provisional exception is validated with the owner, with withdrawals supported by filed new evidence and disputes ruled by the lead.

checklist.step: Establish root cause and quantify the affected population
actions: For each confirmed exception, trace back to the control that failed: notice matrix not refreshed, template not rebound, SLA row wrong, transmittal not swept, business unit missed the internal SLA, handler untrained.
Quantify the exposure beyond the sample — the number of consumers who received the defective notice or the number of complaints handled under the wrong window.
Extrapolate the timing deviation rate to the population and state the projected number of late responses.
Cross-reference each root cause to the checklist item that owns it (C01, C02, C03, C04 or C05).
checklist.done: every confirmed exception carries a named failed control, a quantified affected population, a projected population impact and an owning item.

checklist.step: Rate the issues and draft the report within 10 business days of fieldwork close
actions: Rate each issue: missing notice or wrong DOI contact block High; late responses above 2% of the sample High; record-keeping gaps Medium; formatting-only defects below 5% Low.
Draft the report with scope, criteria source, populations, sample sizes and method, exception counts and rates, root causes and projected population impact.
State the overall opinion on whether complaint notices and response timing meet the requirement across the 51 jurisdictions.
Issue the draft to management within 10 business days of fieldwork close and log the issue date.
checklist.done: a rated draft report with scope, method, exception rates, root causes and an overall opinion is issued within 10 business days of fieldwork close.

checklist.step: Agree management action plans with owners and dates
actions: Return a written response to each issue within 15 business days naming the action, the accountable owner and a specific due date.
Reject a response that only accepts the finding — every High issue needs a dated action and a stated interim control until it lands.
Where management accepts the risk instead, require the Head of Compliance's written rationale and route it to the Audit Committee.
Link each action to the corresponding C01, C03 or C04 change record so the fix is traceable.
checklist.done: every issue has a written management response within 15 business days with a named owner, dated action or an escalated risk acceptance.

checklist.step: Issue the final report and take it to the Audit Committee
actions: Issue the final report within 30 business days of fieldwork close, incorporating management responses verbatim.
Present the opinion, High issues, projected population impact and any risk acceptance to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
Copy the report to the Head of Compliance and the Compliance Committee so the C05 theme programme picks up the drivers.
Record the committee's decisions and any directed action in the minutes and the audit platform.
checklist.done: the final report is issued within 30 business days, presented to the Audit Committee and copied into the compliance theme programme.

checklist.step: Follow up every action to evidenced closure
actions: Open a follow-up task 90 days after each action's due date and request the closure evidence — the released notice edition, the configuration export, the completion figures, the corrected complaint files.
Re-test a small sample against the same criteria row rather than closing on the evidence pack alone.
Escalate any action past due by 30 days to the Audit Committee chair with the owner named.
Close the action only on the Chief Audit Executive's sign-off and file the closure evidence in the audit file under a 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: every action is re-tested at 90 days, escalated at 30 days past due and closed only on inspected evidence with a 7-year retained file.

testing.step: Build the population of audit coverage and workpapers
actions: Extract the REG-027 audit file: planning memo, criteria matrix, population extracts, sampling documentation, test workpapers, issues and management action plans.
Build the coverage grid of 51 jurisdictions against content tested and timing tested to see what the audit actually reached.
List any jurisdiction with no content test and no timing test as a coverage gap before reviewing conclusions.
Record the extraction date and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: the audit file is extracted, a 51-jurisdiction coverage grid is built and coverage gaps are listed before any conclusion is reviewed.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit's populations to source systems
actions: Re-run the timing population query against the complaint case data for the audit year and compare the row count to the audit's population.
Re-run the content population against the live template list and the document archive and compare cell counts.
Confirm the audit reconciled its population to the NAIC State Based Systems and state portal inbound lists rather than only to management's register.
Treat an understated population as a scope defect that undermines every rate the report quotes.
testing.done: the audit's timing and content populations are re-derived from source and agree, or the understatement is quantified as a scope defect.

testing.step: Draw a sample of the audit's own workpapers
actions: Take 100% of workpapers supporting a High-rated issue and 100% supporting a withdrawn exception.
Add 15 passed-sample workpapers by seeded random selection across content and timing tests.
Record the seed, population and draw date in the review workpaper.
Pull the underlying evidence attached to each selected workpaper.
testing.done: the workpaper sample is reproducible and covers all High issues and withdrawn exceptions plus a random selection of passes.

testing.step: Re-perform the audit's key judgement on the sampled workpapers
actions: For sampled timing workpapers, open the transmittal image and the transmission proof yourself and recompute the due date and the days early or late.
For sampled content workpapers, compare the annotated document image to the regulator's current published notice requirement independently.
Compare your conclusion to the auditor's; a pass recorded on a document that actually fails is the most serious result available here.
Record each re-performance with the evidence you relied on.
testing.done: each sampled workpaper carries an independent re-performance with an agree/disagree conclusion and its supporting evidence.

testing.step: Test the currency of the audit criteria themselves
actions: Take 15 criteria rows and read the cited source yourself, including the Alaska complaint-record requirement, Arizona's 15 working days and California 10 CCR 2695.5(b).
Confirm the criterion matches the source as it read during the audit year, not as it reads today, and that the capture date sits within the audit period.
Confirm the criteria matrix was built independently rather than copied from the REG-027-C03 SLA table — a criterion inherited from the control being tested is not independent.
List any criterion that is stale, misquoted or inherited.
testing.done: 15 criteria rows are traced to primary source with independence confirmed, and stale, misquoted or inherited criteria are listed.

testing.step: Recompute the sampling maths and the projected impact
actions: Recompute the sample size implied by 90% confidence and a 5% tolerable deviation rate against the stated population and compare to what was drawn.
Re-draw the sample from the recorded seed and confirm the same items are selected.
Recompute the deviation rate and the projection to the population, and compare to the report's stated projected impact.
Confirm the sample was not expanded or reduced after results were seen, by checking the plan approval date against the draw date.
testing.done: sample size, re-draw, deviation rate and projection all reconcile, with the plan approval confirmed as pre-dating the draw.

testing.step: Test that exceptions were not lost between testing and reporting
actions: Count the confirmed exceptions across the test workpapers and compare to the exception counts stated in the report.
For each withdrawn exception, inspect the new evidence filed and confirm it genuinely resolves the point rather than explaining it.
Confirm every High-rated criterion breach appears as an issue in the report with the affected population quantified.
List any exception that appears in a workpaper but not in the report.
testing.done: workpaper exception counts reconcile to the report, withdrawals are supported by filed evidence, and dropped exceptions are listed.

testing.step: Test the reporting and follow-up timetable and the action closures
actions: Recompute the milestone dates: planning memo by 31 January, fieldwork close, draft within 10 business days, management response within 15, final within 30, and compare to the logged dates.
For each closed management action, open the claimed closure evidence and confirm the 90-day re-test was actually performed and documented.
Confirm actions past due by 30 days were escalated to the Audit Committee chair with the owner named.
Treat an action closed without a documented re-test as a follow-up failure.
testing.done: every reporting milestone is recomputed against the logged dates and every closed action is confirmed to have a documented 90-day re-test.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the workpaper or milestone, defect type (coverage gap, understated population, inherited criterion, sampling defect, dropped exception, unevidenced closure) and its effect on the report's conclusion.
Assign a root cause — criteria copied from the control, population taken from management, sample expanded after results, follow-up closed on assertion — and an owner in Internal Audit.
Set a remediation date before the next annual cycle's planning memo so the fix lands in next year's programme.
Where a coverage gap or understated population materially changes a rate, require the affected testing to be re-performed rather than noted.
testing.done: every exception carries the workpaper, defect type, effect on the conclusion, root cause, owner and a remediation date before the next planning memo.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the jurisdiction coverage rate, the workpaper re-performance agreement rate and the count of dropped or unevidenced items.
State the conclusion on whether the REG-027 audit itself can be relied on as evidence of compliance across the 51 jurisdictions, with workpaper references.
Have a reviewer who performed none of the sampled audit testing — an external quality assessor or an auditor from another engagement — sign the review as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any re-performance requirement to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the review in the compliance evidence repository under a 7-year label.
testing.done: a signed review states coverage, re-performance agreement, dropped items, a reliance conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date.
